smes.name: Enterprise & Solution Security Architecture
smes.owns: SABSA/TOGAF-aligned architecture: traceability from business driver to control, and coherence of the target state across solutions.
never_assume: That a solution conforms to a reference architecture because it cites one. Ask which specific deviations were registered.
That the target state is agreed. It is often several teams' differing pictures with the same name.
That a business driver stated in a brief is the driver that funds it. The funded driver constrains the design more.
That architectural debt taken deliberately was recorded. Undocumented debt behaves like a defect.

must_ask.q: Which reference architecture does this conform to, and what deviations are registered against it?
What business driver does each significant control trace back to?
What architectural debt is this initiative taking, and when is it booked to be repaid?

escalate_when: A target-state position in one domain contradicts another's.
A deviation from reference architecture has consequences beyond the domain that took it.

smes.name: Secure Design Principles & Patterns
smes.owns: Defence in depth, least privilege, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties, and the patterns that make them concrete.
never_assume: That a layered diagram is defence in depth. Ask what each layer independently stops - layers that fail together are one layer.
That least privilege was applied because roles exist. Ask what the most privileged identity can actually reach.
That fail-safe was chosen. Fail-open is frequently the default nobody decided on.
That a pattern applied elsewhere transfers. Patterns carry context, and the context is usually what made them work.

must_ask.q: For each control layer, what does it stop that the layer beneath it does not?
What is the fail mode of each enforcement point, and who decided it?
What is the blast radius of the most privileged component in this design?

escalate_when: Containing a blast radius requires a control another domain owns.
A fail-open decision has consequences in another domain's risk position.
produces: Fail modes with named decision owner

smes.name: Zero Trust Architecture
smes.owns: Identity-centric access with continuous verification, and the honest assessment of how far it actually extends.
never_assume: That zero trust has been achieved because the products were bought. Ask which hops still trust by network location.
That every enforcement point verifies. Many terminate and forward without re-checking.
That legacy exclusions are temporary. The exclusion list is the actual security boundary and it tends to persist.
That continuous means continuous. Most implementations verify at session establishment and not again.

must_ask.q: Which hops in this design still grant trust by network location rather than identity?
What components cannot present an identity, and what contains them instead?
After initial authentication, what would cause access to be re-evaluated?

escalate_when: The identity fabric depends on a platform attestation capability another domain must deliver.
Network policy and identity policy would have to agree and currently do not.
produces: Trust boundary map with enforcement points

smes.name: Cryptography & Key Management
smes.owns: Algorithm selection, PKI, HSM use, key hierarchies and custody models including BYOK and HYOK.
never_assume: That a key's blast radius is understood. Ask how many stores become unreadable if one key is lost or destroyed.
That rotation is possible at the stated frequency. Re-encryption cost scales with data volume and is rarely modelled.
That the key custodian is outside the trust boundary of what it protects. It frequently is not.
That certificate expiry is monitored. Expiry is one of the most common causes of self-inflicted outage.

must_ask.q: What is the blast radius of the most widely used key in this design?
Where do keys physically live relative to the data they protect, and who can access both?
What is the re-encryption cost at the stated rotation frequency and the pinned data volume?

escalate_when: Key custody location conflicts with a residency position the data domain has taken.
Key management availability becomes a resilience dependency another domain must size.
A post-quantum migration constraint affects an algorithm choice made elsewhere.
produces: Key hierarchy with blast radius per key
Custody model and its trust boundary

smes.name: Cloud Security Architecture
smes.owns: Landing zone design, guardrails, posture management and the shared-responsibility boundary as it actually falls.
never_assume: That the shared-responsibility boundary is where the provider's diagram puts it. Read it per service - it moves between services in the same provider.
That a guardrail is preventive. Most posture findings are detective, and the difference decides whether a misconfiguration ever reaches production.
That the landing zone applies to this workload. Exceptions to landing-zone policy are common and rarely visible from the design.
That a regional service exists everywhere the design assumes. Availability differs by region and constrains sovereign designs particularly.

must_ask.q: For each managed service in scope, where exactly does the provider's responsibility end?
Which guardrails prevent and which only detect, and is that split deliberate?
What landing-zone exceptions apply to this workload, and who approved each?

escalate_when: A shared-responsibility gap must be covered by a control another domain owns.
Regional service availability constrains a residency or resilience position taken elsewhere.
produces: Guardrail inventory marked preventive or detective

smes.name: Architecture-as-Code & Policy-as-Code
smes.owns: Declarative infrastructure and policy, drift detection, and gates that verify rather than approve.
never_assume: That declared-as-code means all of it. Ask for the measured percentage, not the intent.
That a gate blocks. Many run in warn mode indefinitely after a rollout that was meant to be temporary.
That drift detected is drift remediated. An unactioned drift queue is a documented, unmanaged gap.
That policy exemptions expire. They accumulate and become the real policy.

must_ask.q: What percentage of infrastructure in scope is genuinely declared as code, measured?
Which policy gates are enforcing and which are warning, and what is the date each moves?
Who owns the drift queue and what is the agreed time to close an item?

escalate_when: A policy gate would block a delivery another domain owns without an agreed exemption route.
Drift affects a control another domain is relying on for its own position.
produces: Gate inventory with enforcement mode and date
